newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTOR RACING-BERGER WINS FIRST RACE BACK AFTER SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BERGER WINS FIRST RACE BACK AFTER SURGERY.

text.p: Austrian veteran Gerhard Berger completed a perfect return to Formula One motor racing on Sunday when he won the German Grand Prix for Benetton.
It was the 37-year-old driver's first victory for exactly three years, since he triumphed for Ferrari at Hockenheim in 1994.

Berger, who missed the last three races following sinus surgery, enjoyed his first win since he returned to Benetton at the beginning of last year and the 10th of his career, ending Benetton's long wait for their first triumph since double world champion Michael Schumacher left the team at the end of 1995.
Schumacher, who leads the world title race this year, finished second on home soil in his Ferrari, 17.5 seconds behind Berger.
But with his title rival Canadian Jacques Villeneuve spinning out of the race after 34 of the 45 laps, Schumacher opened up a 10-point gap at the top.
To complete a good day for the 138,000 crowd, a Mercedes-Benz-powered McLaren car driven by Finland's Mika Hakkinen finished third.
Hakkinen came home ahead of Italian Jarno Trulli in a Prost, Schumacher's 22-year-old younger brother Ralf in a Jordan and Frenchman Jean Alesi in the second Benetton.
The Williams team suffered a bad day with local hope Heinz-Harald Frentzen crashing out with a puncture after one lap and Villeneuve retiring.
This meant they scored no points and Ferrari consolidated their lead in the constructors' championship.
